card.name: Negative before inotropic or chronotropic effects
card.fires_on: The word "negative" right before "inotropic" or "chronotropic" in drug interaction text about heart drugs such as verapamil, flecainide and beta blockers. It also fires weakly on a few other cardiac wording spots like "depression of" the ST segment.

modes.label: Negative inotropic/chronotropic
modes.description: The word "negative" modifying inotropic or chronotropic effects in heart-drug interaction statements.
modes.example: Concomitant therapy with flecainide and verapamil may result in additive<< negative>> inotropic effect and prolongation of atr

modes.label: Other cardiac wording
modes.description: Occasional words within ECG or rhythm descriptions, such as "of" after depression or the middle of "nonsustained".
modes.example: prolongation of the PR interval and depression<< of>> the ST segment on the electrocardi

card.writes: It promotes odd unrelated tokens and suppresses "pulse" words, so the output effect is weak and unclear.
card.plain: It lights up on the word "negative" when a heart drug is said to weaken the force or rate of the heartbeat.
